sources.citation: Clendon, Mark. 2014. Worrorra: a language of the north-west Kimberley coast. Adelaide: University of Adelaide Press.
sources.note: Mentions Umiida (north side of Yampi Peninsula) and Unggarrangu (south side) only geographically, p.5, as Wororic varieties; no data on them. For the sister language Worrorra itself, section 2.6.2 pp.38-46: stress non-phonemic, attracted to long vowels and to the penult, with global rhythmic readjustment.

sources.citation: McGregor, William B. & Alan Rumsey. 2009. Worrorran revisited: the case for genetic relations among languages of the Northern Kimberley region of Western Australia. (Pacific Linguistics 600.) Canberra: Pacific Linguistics. hdl 1885/50063
sources.note: Ch.4 Phonology (pp.20-34) is a comparative segmental inventory/reconstruction; states full phonologies exist only for Worrorra, Ngarinyin, Gunin/Kwini, Wunambal. Table 2 (p.4): Umiida data sources = Capell & Coate 1984 + Coate mss n.d.a 'Umida', n.d.b 'Umida language: Sam Wulugudja'; Unggarrangu = Capell & Coate 1984 + Coate n.d.a. Only stress remark is incidental, p.22, about Unggumi mid vowels being rare 'especially within initial stressed syllables' (presupposes initial stress in Worrorran citation forms). Nothing on Umiida or Unggarrangu stress.

sources.note: Umiida/Unggarrangu mentioned only geographically; nothing on their phonology.

sources.citation: Capell, A. & H.H.J. Coate. 1984. Comparative studies in Northern Kimberley languages. (Pacific Linguistics C-69.) Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Ch.1 'Preliminary: phonological principles' (pp.7-17) covers phonemic systems, syllable types, morphophonemics; no stress section. Umida and Unggarangi appear only in comparative morphology (pronouns, verb classes p.179, interrogatives, negatives). Incidental stress remarks concern Worora/Ngarinjin ('the fixity of the stress is noticeable also, even if it has to fall four syllables back from the end', kinship-term discussion; 'one of the very rare accents on a final syllable', Ngarinjin dialect forms). Silent on Umida/Unggarangi stress.
